-- APPROACH (advisory blueprint / proof-idea guidance; the kernel verifies every step):
-- # Resource allocation — exact envy-freeness is impossible for indivisible goods, but a round-robin allocation is envy-free up to one good (EF1)
--
-- Opens a **resource allocation / computational economics** domain — how to divide indivisible goods (course seats,
-- donated organs, shared compute, spectrum lots, tasks) fairly when no split of a single item is possible. Exact
-- envy-freeness — no agent prefers another's bundle — is the classical ideal, but with indivisible goods it can be
-- flatly unachievable (two agents, one good). The result that made algorithmic fair division tractable is the
-- relaxation **EF1**, envy-free up to one good: no agent envies another once a single good is removed from the
-- other's bundle, and an EF1 allocation always exists and is efficiently computable. This is the library's first
-- result over a discrete allocation of indivisible items with additive valuations — a mechanism institutions run on
-- (matching, course allocation, cloud scheduling), and the fairness standard the field actually deploys.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **additive valuations** — each agent assigns a nonnegative
-- value to each item and values a bundle by the sum of its items' values; (2) an **allocation partitions the items**
-- — every item goes to exactly one agent; (3) for the achievability, a **round-robin picking sequence** in a fixed
-- agent order — in each round every agent takes a most-valued remaining item. Surface where each is used. Model the
-- items as a `Finset` (or a list) and the valuations over an ordered field / ordered semiring; do **not** collapse to
-- a fixed decidable integer instance, and do not restrict to a single fixed profile — the quantification over
-- arbitrary additive profiles is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap, never a fake closure. Probe Mathlib's
-- `Finset.sum` machinery and the banked list-fold patterns rather than re-deriving them.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- ef1_allocation_theory_v2.lean
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Valuation**: an agent's nonnegative value for each item; the value of a bundle is the sum over its items.
-- - **Allocation**: an assignment of each item to one of the agents (the bundles partition the items).
-- - **Envies**: agent `i` envies agent `j` when `i` values `j`'s bundle strictly more than its own.
-- - **EnvyFree**: no agent envies another.
-- - **EnvyFreeUpToOneGood (EF1)**: for every ordered pair of agents `i, j` with `j`'s bundle nonempty, there is an
--   item `g` in `j`'s bundle such that `i` values its own bundle at least as much as `i` values `j`'s bundle with `g`
--   removed.
-- - **DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood (the PAIRWISE EF1 relation — define this)**: agent `i` does not envy agent `j` up to one
--   good when either `j`'s bundle is empty, or there is an item `g` in `j`'s bundle with
--   `bundleValue i (bundle i) ≥ bundleValue i ((bundle j).erase g)`. EF1 is exactly: this holds for every ordered
--   pair. State the pairwise dominance⟹EF1 lemma with THIS as its conclusion — never a placeholder like `∃ g, True`.
-- - **RoundRobin**: given a fixed order on the agents, the allocation built by repeated rounds in which each agent, in
--   turn, takes a most-valued item among those still unallocated.
-- - **SequentiallyDominates**: agent `i`'s sequence of picks dominates agent `j`'s for `i`'s valuation when, pick for
--   pick in each round, `i`'s pick is worth at least as much to `i` as `j`'s pick in that round.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider agents dividing a finite set of indivisible goods under additive valuations. The claim has two parts.
-- First, exact envy-freeness is not always achievable: there is a profile — two agents and a single valued good —
-- for which every allocation leaves some agent envious, so no envy-free allocation exists. Second, envy-freeness up to
-- one good is always achievable: for **any** additive profile, the round-robin allocation in a fixed agent order is
-- EF1 — every agent, after removing a single good from any other's bundle, no longer envies it. So EF1 is the
-- attainable relaxation of envy-freeness for indivisible goods, and the round-robin procedure realizes it. Surface
-- that the achievability uses additivity and the round-robin pick rule, and that EF1 genuinely relaxes envy-freeness:
-- an envy-free allocation is EF1, but not conversely.
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Exact envy-freeness can fail: for the profile with two agents and one good both value positively, every
--   allocation gives the good to one agent, and the other, holding nothing, envies — so no allocation is envy-free.
-- - Envy-freeness implies EF1: if no agent envies another, then removing any one good from another's bundle only
--   lowers its value, so the no-envy inequality still holds — every envy-free allocation is EF1.
-- - Sequential dominance implies EF1 between a pair — conclude exactly `DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood i j` (NOT `∃ g, True`):
--   if agent `i`'s picks sequentially dominate agent `j`'s for `i`'s
--   valuation, then dropping `j`'s first-round pick leaves `i` not envying `j` — the remaining picks pair up with
--   `i`'s own picks, each at least as valuable to `i`, so the bundle sums compare (a telescoped `Finset.sum`
--   inequality).
-- - Round-robin is EF1: for any additive profile, the round-robin allocation makes each earlier-in-order agent
--   sequentially dominate each later one (it picks first each round, over the same remaining pool), and the reverse
--   direction is covered by dropping the dominating agent's extra first pick — so every pair is EF1, hence the
--   allocation is EF1.
--
-- ## Idea
-- Model the items as a `Finset` and each agent's valuation as a nonnegative weight per item; a bundle's value is
-- `Finset.sum` of its items' weights. The impossibility witness is concrete and small: two agents (`Fin 2`), one good
-- of value `1` to both; the agent without it values its own bundle `0` and the other's `1`. **Model the good as a
-- real item — a one-element `Finset` over the item type (e.g. `({0} : Finset (Fin 1))` or a named item), NOT the unit
-- type**: a `def OneGood := PUnit` / `abbrev … := Unit` is a degenerate constant shell (the good carries no structure
-- tying it to the valuation) and the def-shell firewall rejects it — correctly, because the impossibility must hold
-- over an actual item, not an abstract point. Envy-free-implies-EF1 is
-- monotonicity of `Finset.sum` under removing a nonnegative-weight element. The load-bearing lemma is
-- sequential-dominance ⟹ EF1: line up `i`'s picks with `j`'s picks round by round; because `i` picked a most-valued
-- remaining item before `j` in each shared round, `i`'s `t`-th pick is `≥` (to `i`) `j`'s `t`-th pick, so summing and
-- dropping `j`'s first pick gives `v_i(A_i) ≥ v_i(A_j ∖ {first})` — a telescoped sum comparison, one induction over
-- the rounds. Round-robin then instantiates the dominance from the pick rule. Keep the valuations as parameters over
-- the field, carry additivity and nonnegativity, and do not fix a decidable carrier or a single profile. This is a
-- frontier target — the round-robin construction is a real lift; the impossibility, the EF⊆EF1 direction, and the
-- dominance⟹EF1 core are the achievable spine if the full construction resists.

  cases l with
  | nil =>
      rw [← h] at hs
      simpa using hs
  | cons a t =>

      simp

      (ys.map fun g => v.value g).sum ≤ (xs.map fun g => v.value g).sum

  | [], y :: ys, hlen, _ => by simp at hlen

        simpa using hle 0 (by simp) (by simp)

          v.value (iPicks.get ⟨n, hi⟩) := by
    intro n hj hi

-- APPROACH (advisory blueprint / proof-idea guidance; the kernel verifies every step):
-- # Resource allocation — exact envy-freeness is impossible for indivisible goods, but a round-robin allocation is envy-free up to one good (EF1)
--
-- Opens a **resource allocation / computational economics** domain — how to divide indivisible goods (course seats,
-- donated organs, shared compute, spectrum lots, tasks) fairly when no split of a single item is possible. Exact
-- envy-freeness — no agent prefers another's bundle — is the classical ideal, but with indivisible goods it can be
-- flatly unachievable (two agents, one good). The result that made algorithmic fair division tractable is the
-- relaxation **EF1**, envy-free up to one good: no agent envies another once a single good is removed from the
-- other's bundle, and an EF1 allocation always exists and is efficiently computable. This is the library's first
-- result over a discrete allocation of indivisible items with additive valuations — a mechanism institutions run on
-- (matching, course allocation, cloud scheduling), and the fairness standard the field actually deploys.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **additive valuations** — each agent assigns a nonnegative
-- value to each item and values a bundle by the sum of its items' values; (2) an **allocation partitions the items**
-- — every item goes to exactly one agent; (3) for the achievability, a **round-robin picking sequence** in a fixed
-- agent order — in each round every agent takes a most-valued remaining item. Surface where each is used. Model the
-- items as a `Finset` (or a list) and the valuations over an ordered field / ordered semiring; do **not** collapse to
-- a fixed decidable integer instance, and do not restrict to a single fixed profile — the quantification over
-- arbitrary additive profiles is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap, never a fake closure. Probe Mathlib's
-- `Finset.sum` machinery and the banked list-fold patterns rather than re-deriving them.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- ef1_allocation_theory_v2.lean
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Valuation**: an agent's nonnegative value for each item; the value of a bundle is the sum over its items.
-- - **Allocation**: an assignment of each item to one of the agents (the bundles partition the items).
-- - **Envies**: agent `i` envies agent `j` when `i` values `j`'s bundle strictly more than its own.
-- - **EnvyFree**: no agent envies another.
-- - **EnvyFreeUpToOneGood (EF1)**: for every ordered pair of agents `i, j` with `j`'s bundle nonempty, there is an
--   item `g` in `j`'s bundle such that `i` values its own bundle at least as much as `i` values `j`'s bundle with `g`
--   removed.
-- - **DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood (the PAIRWISE EF1 relation — define this)**: agent `i` does not envy agent `j` up to one
--   good when either `j`'s bundle is empty, or there is an item `g` in `j`'s bundle with
--   `bundleValue i (bundle i) ≥ bundleValue i ((bundle j).erase g)`. EF1 is exactly: this holds for every ordered
--   pair. State the pairwise dominance⟹EF1 lemma with THIS as its conclusion — never a placeholder like `∃ g, True`.
-- - **RoundRobin**: given a fixed order on the agents, the allocation built by repeated rounds in which each agent, in
--   turn, takes a most-valued item among those still unallocated.
-- - **SequentiallyDominates**: agent `i`'s sequence of picks dominates agent `j`'s for `i`'s valuation when, pick for
--   pick in each round, `i`'s pick is worth at least as much to `i` as `j`'s pick in that round.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider agents dividing a finite set of indivisible goods under additive valuations. The claim has two parts.
-- First, exact envy-freeness is not always achievable: there is a profile — two agents and a single valued good —
-- for which every allocation leaves some agent envious, so no envy-free allocation exists. Second, envy-freeness up to
-- one good is always achievable: for **any** additive profile, the round-robin allocation in a fixed agent order is
-- EF1 — every agent, after removing a single good from any other's bundle, no longer envies it. So EF1 is the
-- attainable relaxation of envy-freeness for indivisible goods, and the round-robin procedure realizes it. Surface
-- that the achievability uses additivity and the round-robin pick rule, and that EF1 genuinely relaxes envy-freeness:
-- an envy-free allocation is EF1, but not conversely.
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Exact envy-freeness can fail: for the profile with two agents and one good both value positively, every
--   allocation gives the good to one agent, and the other, holding nothing, envies — so no allocation is envy-free.
-- - Envy-freeness implies EF1: if no agent envies another, then removing any one good from another's bundle only
--   lowers its value, so the no-envy inequality still holds — every envy-free allocation is EF1.
-- - Sequential dominance implies EF1 between a pair — conclude exactly `DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood i j` (NOT `∃ g, True`):
--   if agent `i`'s picks sequentially dominate agent `j`'s for `i`'s
--   valuation, then dropping `j`'s first-round pick leaves `i` not envying `j` — the remaining picks pair up with
--   `i`'s own picks, each at least as valuable to `i`, so the bundle sums compare (a telescoped `Finset.sum`
--   inequality).
-- - Round-robin is EF1: for any additive profile, the round-robin allocation makes each earlier-in-order agent
--   sequentially dominate each later one (it picks first each round, over the same remaining pool), and the reverse
--   direction is covered by dropping the dominating agent's extra first pick — so every pair is EF1, hence the
--   allocation is EF1.
--

-- Model the items as a `Finset` and each agent's valuation as a nonnegative weight per item; a bundle's value is
-- `Finset.sum` of its items' weights. The impossibility witness is concrete and small: two agents (`Fin 2`), one good

-- over an actual item, not an abstract point. Envy-free-implies-EF1 is

-- sequential-dominance ⟹ EF1: line up `i`'s picks with `j`'s picks round by round; because `i` picked a most-valued
-- remaining item before `j` in each shared round, `i`'s `t`-th pick is `≥` (to `i`) `j`'s `t`-th pick, so summing and
-- dropping `j`'s first pick gives `v_i(A_i) ≥ v_i(A_j ∖ {first})` — a telescoped sum comparison, one induction over
-- the rounds. Round-robin then instantiates the dominance from the pick rule. Keep the valuations as parameters over
-- the field, carry additivity and nonnegativity, and do not fix a decidable carrier or a single profile. This is a
-- frontier target — the round-robin construction is a real lift; the impossibility, the EF⊆EF1 direction, and the

namespace EF1Allocation

variable {Agent Item K : Type*}

section OrderedField

variable [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K]

structure Valuation (Item K : Type*) [Zero K] [LE K] where
  value : Item → K
  nonneg : ∀ g : Item, 0 ≤ value g

def bundleValue (v : Valuation Item K) (bundle : Finset Item) : K :=
  Finset.sum bundle fun g => v.value g

structure Allocation (Agent Item : Type*) where
  owner : Item → Agent

def bundle [DecidableEq Agent]
    (goods : Finset Item) (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i : Agent) : Finset Item :=
  goods.filter fun g => allocation.owner g = i

def Envies [DecidableEq Agent]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i j : Agent) : Prop :=
  bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation i) <
    bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation j)

def EnvyFree [DecidableEq Agent]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Agent, ¬ Envies profile goods allocation i j

abbrev TwoAgent := Fin 2

abbrev OneGoodItem := Fin 1

def oneGoodSet : Finset OneGoodItem :=
  {(0 : OneGoodItem)}

def oneGoodPositiveValuation : Valuation OneGoodItem K :=
  { value := fun _ => 1
    nonneg := by intro _; norm_num }

def twoAgentOneGoodProfile : TwoAgent → Valuation OneGoodItem K :=
  fun _ => oneGoodPositiveValuation

-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Valuation**: an agent's nonnegative value for each item; the value of a bundle is the sum over its items.
-- - **Allocation**: an assignment of each item to one of the agents (the bundles partition the items).
-- - **Envies**: agent `i` envies agent `j` when `i` values `j`'s bundle strictly more than its own.
-- - **EnvyFree**: no agent envies another.
-- - **EnvyFreeUpToOneGood (EF1)**: for every ordered pair of agents `i, j` with `j`'s bundle nonempty, there is an
--   item `g` in `j`'s bundle such that `i` values its own bundle at least as much as `i` values `j`'s bundle with `g`
--   removed.
-- - **DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood (the PAIRWISE EF1 relation — define this)**: agent `i` does not envy agent `j` up to one
--   good when either `j`'s bundle is empty, or there is an item `g` in `j`'s bundle with
--   `bundleValue i (bundle i) ≥ bundleValue i ((bundle j).erase g)`. EF1 is exactly: this holds for every ordered
--   pair. State the pairwise dominance⟹EF1 lemma with THIS as its conclusion — never a placeholder like `∃ g, True`.
-- - **RoundRobin**: given a fixed order on the agents, the allocation built by repeated rounds in which each agent, in
--   turn, takes a most-valued item among those still unallocated.
-- - **SequentiallyDominates**: agent `i`'s sequence of picks dominates agent `j`'s for `i`'s valuation when, pick for
--   pick in each round, `i`'s pick is worth at least as much to `i` as `j`'s pick in that round.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider agents dividing a finite set of indivisible goods under additive valuations. The claim has two parts.
-- First, exact envy-freeness is not always achievable: there is a profile — two agents and a single valued good —
-- for which every allocation leaves some agent envious, so no envy-free allocation exists. Second, envy-freeness up to
-- one good is always achievable: for **any** additive profile, the round-robin allocation in a fixed agent order is
-- EF1 — every agent, after removing a single good from any other's bundle, no longer envies it. So EF1 is the
-- attainable relaxation of envy-freeness for indivisible goods, and the round-robin procedure realizes it. Surface
-- that the achievability uses additivity and the round-robin pick rule, and that EF1 genuinely relaxes envy-freeness:
-- an envy-free allocation is EF1, but not conversely.
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Exact envy-freeness can fail: for the profile with two agents and one good both value positively, every
--   allocation gives the good to one agent, and the other, holding nothing, envies — so no allocation is envy-free.
-- - Envy-freeness implies EF1: if no agent envies another, then removing any one good from another's bundle only
--   lowers its value, so the no-envy inequality still holds — every envy-free allocation is EF1.
-- - Sequential dominance implies EF1 between a pair — conclude exactly `DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood i j` (NOT `∃ g, True`):
--   if agent `i`'s picks sequentially dominate agent `j`'s for `i`'s

--   `i`'s own picks, each at least as valuable to `i`, so the bundle sums compare (a telescoped `Finset.sum`
--   inequality).
-- - Round-robin is EF1: for any additive profile, the round-robin allocation makes each earlier-in-order agent
--   sequentially dominate each later one (it picks first each round, over the same remaining pool), and the reverse
--   direction is covered by dropping the dominating agent's extra first pick — so every pair is EF1, hence the
--   allocation is EF1.

          v.value (iPicks.get ⟨n, hi⟩) := by
    intro n hj hi
    have hj' : n + 1 < jPicks.length := by
      simp only [List.length_tail] at hj
      omega
    rcases hdom.2.2 n hj' with ⟨hi', hle⟩
    simpa [List.get_tail] using hle
  have hlist :
      (jPicks.tail.map fun g => v.value g).sum ≤
        (iPicks.map fun g => v.value g).sum :=
    list_sum_le_of_get v htail_len hpoint
  have hjnd : jPicks.tail.Nodup := hdom.2.1.tail
  calc
    bundleValue v jPicks.tail.toFinset

          simpa [bundleValue] using
            (List.sum_toFinset (fun g => v.value g) hjnd)
    _ ≤ (iPicks.map fun g => v.value g).sum := hlist
    _ = bundleValue v iPicks.toFinset := by
          simpa [bundleValue] using
            (List.sum_toFinset (fun g => v.value g) hdom.1).symm

    (v : Valuation Item K) {iPicks jPicks : List Item}

  value : Item → K

  Finset.sum bundle fun g => v.value g

  owner : Item → Agent

    (goods : Finset Item) (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i : Agent) : Finset Item :=

    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i j : Agent) : Prop :=
  bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation i) <

    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Agent, ¬ Envies profile goods allocation i j

-- APPROACH (advisory blueprint / proof-idea guidance; the kernel verifies every step):
-- # Resource allocation — exact envy-freeness is impossible for indivisible goods, but a round-robin allocation is envy-free up to one good (EF1)
--
-- Opens a **resource allocation / computational economics** domain — how to divide indivisible goods (course seats,
-- donated organs, shared compute, spectrum lots, tasks) fairly when no split of a single item is possible. Exact
-- envy-freeness — no agent prefers another's bundle — is the classical ideal, but with indivisible goods it can be
-- flatly unachievable (two agents, one good). The result that made algorithmic fair division tractable is the
-- relaxation **EF1**, envy-free up to one good: no agent envies another once a single good is removed from the
-- other's bundle, and an EF1 allocation always exists and is efficiently computable. This is the library's first
-- result over a discrete allocation of indivisible items with additive valuations — a mechanism institutions run on
-- (matching, course allocation, cloud scheduling), and the fairness standard the field actually deploys.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **additive valuations** — each agent assigns a nonnegative
-- value to each item and values a bundle by the sum of its items' values; (2) an **allocation partitions the items**
-- — every item goes to exactly one agent; (3) for the achievability, a **round-robin picking sequence** in a fixed
-- agent order — in each round every agent takes a most-valued remaining item. Surface where each is used. Model the
-- items as a `Finset` (or a list) and the valuations over an ordered field / ordered semiring; do **not** collapse to
-- a fixed decidable integer instance, and do not restrict to a single fixed profile — the quantification over
-- arbitrary additive profiles is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap, never a fake closure. Probe Mathlib's
-- `Finset.sum` machinery and the banked list-fold patterns rather than re-deriving them.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- ef1_allocation_theory_v2.lean
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Valuation**: an agent's nonnegative value for each item; the value of a bundle is the sum over its items.
-- - **Allocation**: an assignment of each item to one of the agents (the bundles partition the items).
-- - **Envies**: agent `i` envies agent `j` when `i` values `j`'s bundle strictly more than its own.
-- - **EnvyFree**: no agent envies another.
-- - **EnvyFreeUpToOneGood (EF1)**: for every ordered pair of agents `i, j` with `j`'s bundle nonempty, there is an
--   item `g` in `j`'s bundle such that `i` values its own bundle at least as much as `i` values `j`'s bundle with `g`
--   removed.
-- - **DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood (the PAIRWISE EF1 relation — define this)**: agent `i` does not envy agent `j` up to one
--   good when either `j`'s bundle is empty, or there is an item `g` in `j`'s bundle with
--   `bundleValue i (bundle i) ≥ bundleValue i ((bundle j).erase g)`. EF1 is exactly: this holds for every ordered
--   pair. State the pairwise dominance⟹EF1 lemma with THIS as its conclusion — never a placeholder like `∃ g, True`.
-- - **RoundRobin**: given a fixed order on the agents, the allocation built by repeated rounds in which each agent, in
--   turn, takes a most-valued item among those still unallocated.
-- - **SequentiallyDominates**: agent `i`'s sequence of picks dominates agent `j`'s for `i`'s valuation when, pick for
--   pick in each round, `i`'s pick is worth at least as much to `i` as `j`'s pick in that round.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider agents dividing a finite set of indivisible goods under additive valuations. The claim has two parts.
-- First, exact envy-freeness is not always achievable: there is a profile — two agents and a single valued good —
-- for which every allocation leaves some agent envious, so no envy-free allocation exists. Second, envy-freeness up to
-- one good is always achievable: for **any** additive profile, the round-robin allocation in a fixed agent order is
-- EF1 — every agent, after removing a single good from any other's bundle, no longer envies it. So EF1 is the
-- attainable relaxation of envy-freeness for indivisible goods, and the round-robin procedure realizes it. Surface
-- that the achievability uses additivity and the round-robin pick rule, and that EF1 genuinely relaxes envy-freeness:
-- an envy-free allocation is EF1, but not conversely.
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Exact envy-freeness can fail: for the profile with two agents and one good both value positively, every
--   allocation gives the good to one agent, and the other, holding nothing, envies — so no allocation is envy-free.
-- - Envy-freeness implies EF1: if no agent envies another, then removing any one good from another's bundle only
--   lowers its value, so the no-envy inequality still holds — every envy-free allocation is EF1.
-- - Sequential dominance implies EF1 between a pair — conclude exactly `DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood i j` (NOT `∃ g, True`):
--   if agent `i`'s picks sequentially dominate agent `j`'s for `i`'s
--   valuation, then dropping `j`'s first-round pick leaves `i` not envying `j` — the remaining picks pair up with
--   `i`'s own picks, each at least as valuable to `i`, so the bundle sums compare (a telescoped `Finset.sum`
--   inequality).
-- - Round-robin is EF1: for any additive profile, the round-robin allocation makes each earlier-in-order agent
--   sequentially dominate each later one (it picks first each round, over the same remaining pool), and the reverse
--   direction is covered by dropping the dominating agent's extra first pick — so every pair is EF1, hence the
--   allocation is EF1.
--
-- ## Idea
-- Model the items as a `Finset` and each agent's valuation as a nonnegative weight per item; a bundle's value is
-- `Finset.sum` of its items' weights. The impossibility witness is concrete and small: two agents (`Fin 2`), one good
-- of value `1` to both; the agent without it values its own bundle `0` and the other's `1`. **Model the good as a
-- real item — a one-element `Finset` over the item type (e.g. `({0} : Finset (Fin 1))` or a named item), NOT the unit
-- type**: a `def OneGood := PUnit` / `abbrev … := Unit` is a degenerate constant shell (the good carries no structure
-- tying it to the valuation) and the def-shell firewall rejects it — correctly, because the impossibility must hold
-- over an actual item, not an abstract point. Envy-free-implies-EF1 is
-- monotonicity of `Finset.sum` under removing a nonnegative-weight element. The load-bearing lemma is
-- sequential-dominance ⟹ EF1: line up `i`'s picks with `j`'s picks round by round; because `i` picked a most-valued
-- remaining item before `j` in each shared round, `i`'s `t`-th pick is `≥` (to `i`) `j`'s `t`-th pick, so summing and
-- dropping `j`'s first pick gives `v_i(A_i) ≥ v_i(A_j ∖ {first})` — a telescoped sum comparison, one induction over
-- the rounds. Round-robin then instantiates the dominance from the pick rule. Keep the valuations as parameters over
-- the field, carry additivity and nonnegativity, and do not fix a decidable carrier or a single profile. This is a
-- frontier target — the round-robin construction is a real lift; the impossibility, the EF⊆EF1 direction, and the
-- dominance⟹EF1 core are the achievable spine if the full construction resists.

import Mathlib

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false

namespace EF1Allocation

variable {Agent Item K : Type*}

section OrderedField

variable [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K]

structure Valuation (Item K : Type*) [Zero K] [LE K] where
  value : Item → K
  nonneg : ∀ g : Item, 0 ≤ value g

def bundleValue (v : Valuation Item K) (bundle : Finset Item) : K :=
  Finset.sum bundle fun g => v.value g

structure Allocation (Agent Item : Type*) where
  owner : Item → Agent

def bundle [DecidableEq Agent]
    (goods : Finset Item) (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i : Agent) : Finset Item :=
  goods.filter fun g => allocation.owner g = i

def Envies [DecidableEq Agent]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i j : Agent) : Prop :=
  bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation i) <
    bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation j)

def EnvyFree [DecidableEq Agent]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Agent, ¬ Envies profile goods allocation i j

def DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood [DecidableEq Agent] [DecidableEq Item]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (i j : Agent) : Prop :=
  (bundle goods allocation j).Nonempty →
    ∃ g ∈ bundle goods allocation j,
      bundleValue (profile i) (bundle goods allocation i) ≥
        bundleValue (profile i) ((bundle goods allocation j).erase g)

def EnvyFreeUpToOneGood [DecidableEq Agent] [DecidableEq Item]
    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Agent, DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood profile goods allocation i j

theorem EnvyFree_implies_EnvyFreeUpToOneGood [DecidableEq Agent] [DecidableEq Item]
    {profile : Agent → Valuation Item K} {goods : Finset Item}
    {allocation : Allocation Agent Item}

  | [], _ :: _, hlen, _ => by simp at hlen

          simpa [Nat.succ_eq_add_one] using Nat.succ_lt_succ hx

    intro n hj hi

  cases jPicks with

-- # Resource allocation — exact envy-freeness is impossible for indivisible goods, but a round-robin allocation is envy-free up to one good (EF1)
--
-- Opens a **resource allocation / computational economics** domain — how to divide indivisible goods (course seats,
-- donated organs, shared compute, spectrum lots, tasks) fairly when no split of a single item is possible. Exact
-- envy-freeness — no agent prefers another's bundle — is the classical ideal, but with indivisible goods it can be
-- flatly unachievable (two agents, one good). The result that made algorithmic fair division tractable is the
-- relaxation **EF1**, envy-free up to one good: no agent envies another once a single good is removed from the
-- other's bundle, and an EF1 allocation always exists and is efficiently computable. This is the library's first
-- result over a discrete allocation of indivisible items with additive valuations — a mechanism institutions run on
-- (matching, course allocation, cloud scheduling), and the fairness standard the field actually deploys.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **additive valuations** — each agent assigns a nonnegative
-- value to each item and values a bundle by the sum of its items' values; (2) an **allocation partitions the items**
-- — every item goes to exactly one agent; (3) for the achievability, a **round-robin picking sequence** in a fixed
-- agent order — in each round every agent takes a most-valued remaining item. Surface where each is used. Model the
-- items as a `Finset` (or a list) and the valuations over an ordered field / ordered semiring; do **not** collapse to
-- a fixed decidable integer instance, and do not restrict to a single fixed profile — the quantification over
-- arbitrary additive profiles is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap, never a fake closure. Probe Mathlib's
-- `Finset.sum` machinery and the banked list-fold patterns rather than re-deriving them.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- ef1_allocation_theory_v2.lean
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Valuation**: an agent's nonnegative value for each item; the value of a bundle is the sum over its items.
-- - **Allocation**: an assignment of each item to one of the agents (the bundles partition the items).
-- - **Envies**: agent `i` envies agent `j` when `i` values `j`'s bundle strictly more than its own.
-- - **EnvyFree**: no agent envies another.
-- - **EnvyFreeUpToOneGood (EF1)**: for every ordered pair of agents `i, j` with `j`'s bundle nonempty, there is an
--   item `g` in `j`'s bundle such that `i` values its own bundle at least as much as `i` values `j`'s bundle with `g`
--   removed.
-- - **DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood (the PAIRWISE EF1 relation — define this)**: agent `i` does not envy agent `j` up to one
--   good when either `j`'s bundle is empty, or there is an item `g` in `j`'s bundle with
--   `bundleValue i (bundle i) ≥ bundleValue i ((bundle j).erase g)`. EF1 is exactly: this holds for every ordered
--   pair. State the pairwise dominance⟹EF1 lemma with THIS as its conclusion — never a placeholder like `∃ g, True`.
-- - **RoundRobin**: given a fixed order on the agents, the allocation built by repeated rounds in which each agent, in
--   turn, takes a most-valued item among those still unallocated.
-- - **SequentiallyDominates**: agent `i`'s sequence of picks dominates agent `j`'s for `i`'s valuation when, pick for
--   pick in each round, `i`'s pick is worth at least as much to `i` as `j`'s pick in that round.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider agents dividing a finite set of indivisible goods under additive valuations. The claim has two parts.
-- First, exact envy-freeness is not always achievable: there is a profile — two agents and a single valued good —
-- for which every allocation leaves some agent envious, so no envy-free allocation exists. Second, envy-freeness up to
-- one good is always achievable: for **any** additive profile, the round-robin allocation in a fixed agent order is
-- EF1 — every agent, after removing a single good from any other's bundle, no longer envies it. So EF1 is the
-- attainable relaxation of envy-freeness for indivisible goods, and the round-robin procedure realizes it. Surface
-- that the achievability uses additivity and the round-robin pick rule, and that EF1 genuinely relaxes envy-freeness:
-- an envy-free allocation is EF1, but not conversely.
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Exact envy-freeness can fail: for the profile with two agents and one good both value positively, every
--   allocation gives the good to one agent, and the other, holding nothing, envies — so no allocation is envy-free.
-- - Envy-freeness implies EF1: if no agent envies another, then removing any one good from another's bundle only
--   lowers its value, so the no-envy inequality still holds — every envy-free allocation is EF1.
-- - Sequential dominance implies EF1 between a pair — conclude exactly `DoesNotEnvyUpToOneGood i j` (NOT `∃ g, True`):
--   if agent `i`'s picks sequentially dominate agent `j`'s for `i`'s
--   valuation, then dropping `j`'s first-round pick leaves `i` not envying `j` — the remaining picks pair up with
--   `i`'s own picks, each at least as valuable to `i`, so the bundle sums compare (a telescoped `Finset.sum`
--   inequality).
-- - Round-robin is EF1: for any additive profile, the round-robin allocation makes each earlier-in-order agent
--   sequentially dominate each later one (it picks first each round, over the same remaining pool), and the reverse
--   direction is covered by dropping the dominating agent's extra first pick — so every pair is EF1, hence the
--   allocation is EF1.
--
-- ## Idea
-- Model the items as a `Finset` and each agent's valuation as a nonnegative weight per item; a bundle's value is
-- `Finset.sum` of its items' weights. The impossibility witness is concrete and small: two agents (`Fin 2`), one good
-- of value `1` to both; the agent without it values its own bundle `0` and the other's `1`. **Model the good as a
-- real item — a one-element `Finset` over the item type (e.g. `({0} : Finset (Fin 1))` or a named item), NOT the unit
-- type**: a `def OneGood := PUnit` / `abbrev … := Unit` is a degenerate constant shell (the good carries no structure
-- tying it to the valuation) and the def-shell firewall rejects it — correctly, because the impossibility must hold
-- over an actual item, not an abstract point. Envy-free-implies-EF1 is
-- monotonicity of `Finset.sum` under removing a nonnegative-weight element. The load-bearing lemma is
-- sequential-dominance ⟹ EF1: line up `i`'s picks with `j`'s picks round by round; because `i` picked a most-valued
-- remaining item before `j` in each shared round, `i`'s `t`-th pick is `≥` (to `i`) `j`'s `t`-th pick, so summing and
-- dropping `j`'s first pick gives `v_i(A_i) ≥ v_i(A_j ∖ {first})` — a telescoped sum comparison, one induction over
-- the rounds. Round-robin then instantiates the dominance from the pick rule. Keep the valuations as parameters over
-- the field, carry additivity and nonnegativity, and do not fix a decidable carrier or a single profile. This is a
-- frontier target — the round-robin construction is a real lift; the impossibility, the EF⊆EF1 direction, and the
-- dominance⟹EF1 core are the achievable spine if the full construction resists.

inductive Side where
  | bid
  | ask
  deriving DecidableEq

def opposite : Side → Side
  | Side.bid => Side.ask
  | Side.ask => Side.bid

def betterPrice {K : Type*} [LinearOrder K] : Side → K → K → Prop
  | Side.bid, x, y => y < x
  | Side.ask, x, y => x < y

structure Order (K T : Type*) [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] where
  side : Side
  price : K
  arrival : T
  qty : K
  qty_pos : 0 < qty

                                                                       

structure Book (K T : Type*) [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] where
  bids : List (Order K T)
  asks : List (Order K T)

def emptyBook {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] : Book K T :=
  {
    bids := [],
    asks := []
  }

                                            

def ordersOnSide {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] (book : Book K T) :
    Side → List (Order K T)
  | Side.bid => book.bids
  | Side.ask => book.asks

def restOrder {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K]
    (book : Book K T) (incoming : Order K T) : Book K T :=
  match incoming.side with
  | Side.bid =>
      {
        bids := incoming :: book.bids,
        asks := book.asks
      }
  | Side.ask =>
      {
        bids := book.bids,
        asks := incoming :: book.asks
      }

def bestBid {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] (book : Book K T) : Option K :=
  book.bids.head?.map (fun order => order.price)

                                                                              

def bestAsk {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] (book : Book K T) : Option K :=
  book.asks.head?.map (fun order => order.price)

def PriorityAhead {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [LT T]
    (x y : Order K T) : Prop :=
  x.side = y.side ∧
    (betterPrice x.side x.price y.price ∨
      (x.price = y.price ∧ x.arrival < y.arrival))

def PrioritySorted {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [LT T]
    (orders : List (Order K T)) : Prop :=
  orders.Pairwise PriorityAhead

def Uncrossed {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] (book : Book K T) : Prop :=
  ∀ bid ask, bestBid book = some bid → bestAsk book = some ask → bid < ask

def Marketable {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K]
    (incoming : Order K T) (book : Book K T) : Prop :=
  match incoming.side with
  | Side.bid => ∃ ask, bestAsk book = some ask ∧ ask ≤ incoming.price
  | Side.ask => ∃ bid, bestBid book = some bid ∧ incoming.price ≤ bid

noncomputable def matchInto {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K]
    (book : Book K T) (incoming : Order K T) : Book K T := by
  classical
  exact if Marketable incoming book then book else restOrder book incoming

structure FillEvent (K T : Type*) [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] where
  incoming : Order K T
  resting : Order K T
  qty : K
  qty_pos : 0 < qty

                                                                             
                                                                               
                

                                                                               
                                                                               
                                                                       
  

def FillRespectsPriority {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [LT T]
    (after : Book K T) (fill : FillEvent K T) : Prop :=
  ∀ order ∈ ordersOnSide after fill.resting.side,
    ¬ PriorityAhead order fill.resting

def StrictPriceTimeExecution {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [LT T]
    (after : Book K T) (fills : List (FillEvent K T)) : Prop :=
  ∀ fill ∈ fills, FillRespectsPriority after fill

def cancelOrder {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [DecidableEq T]
    (side : Side) (arrival : T) (book : Book K T) : Book K T :=
  match side with
  | Side.bid =>
      { bids := book.bids.filter (fun order => order.arrival ≠ arrival)
        asks := book.asks }
  | Side.ask =>
      { bids := book.bids
        asks := book.asks.filter (fun order => order.arrival ≠ arrival) }

inductive Operation (K T : Type*) [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] where
  | limit (incoming : Order K T)
  | market (side : Side) (qty : K) (qty_pos : 0 < qty)
  | cancel (side : Side) (arrival : T)

                                       

noncomputable def applyOp {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [DecidableEq T]
    (book : Book K T) : Operation K T → Book K T
  | Operation.limit incoming => matchInto book incoming
  | Operation.market _ _ _ => book
  | Operation.cancel side arrival => cancelOrder side arrival book

noncomputable def postOps {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [DecidableEq T]
    (book : Book K T) (ops : List (Operation K T)) : Book K T :=
  ops.foldl applyOp book

def Reachable {K T : Type*} [Zero K] [LinearOrder K] [DecidableEq T]
    (initial target : Book K T) : Prop :=

  iPicks.Nodup ∧ jPicks.Nodup ∧
    ∀ n (hj : n + 1 < jPicks.length),

        v.value (jPicks.get ⟨n + 1, hj⟩) ≤ v.value (iPicks.get ⟨n, hi⟩)

def pickedItems [DecidableEq Item] (picks : List (Agent × Item)) : Finset Item :=
  (picks.map Prod.snd).toFinset

    (goods : Finset Item) (picks : List (Agent × Item)) (n : Nat) : Finset Item :=
  goods \ ((picks.take n).map Prod.snd).toFinset

  order.Nodup ∧ ∀ i : Agent, i ∈ order

    (profile : Agent → Valuation Item K) (goods : Finset Item)
    (order : List Agent) (picks : List (Agent × Item)) : Prop :=
  ∃ hlen : 0 < order.length,
    CoveredAgentOrder order ∧
      (picks.map Prod.snd).Nodup ∧
        pickedItems (Item := Item) picks = goods ∧
          ∀ n (hn : n < picks.length),
            let pick := picks.get ⟨n, hn⟩
            pick.1 = order.get ⟨n % order.length, Nat.mod_lt n hlen⟩ ∧
              pick.2 ∈ remainingItems goods picks n ∧
                ∀ g ∈ remainingItems goods picks n,
                  (profile pick.1).value g ≤ (profile pick.1).value pick.2

    (allocation : Allocation Agent Item) (picks : List (Agent × Item)) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (hn : n < picks.length),
    allocation.owner (picks.get ⟨n, hn⟩).2 = (picks.get ⟨n, hn⟩).1

    {profile : Agent → Valuation Item K} {goods : Finset Item}
    {order : List Agent} {allocation : Allocation Agent Item}
    {picks : List (Agent × Item)}
    (hlog : PickLogRoundRobin profile goods order picks)
    (hmatch : PickLogMatchesAllocation allocation picks) :
    EnvyFreeUpToOneGood profile goods allocation := by
  (repeat' apply And.intro) <;> (first | assumption | exact?)

-- APPROACH (advisory blueprint / proof-idea guidance; the kernel verifies every step):
-- # Stable matching — deferred acceptance produces a matching with no blocking pair, across any complete proposal run
--
-- Opens the **market design / two-sided matching** frontier — the mechanism that clears the medical-residency match
-- (NRMP), public-school choice, and kidney exchange, and the one whose "intent" is contested in court and in policy
-- (the NRMP faced antitrust litigation over exactly what the match guarantees). The iconic result is Gale–Shapley:
-- run the deferred-acceptance procedure — each unengaged agent proposes down its preference list, each receiver keeps
-- its best proposer so far and rejects the rest — and the outcome is **stable**: no man and woman both strictly
-- prefer each other to the partner the match assigned them. Stability is the property the field means by "the match
-- is fair to participants," and it is what makes a centralized clearinghouse hold together against side deals. This is
-- the library's first result over an **iterative allocation process whose invariant is a monotone tentative
-- assignment** — the deferred-acceptance reachable-state induction, a discrete counterpart of the CLOB matching
-- engine, over preference orders rather than prices.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **strict preferences** — each man strictly ranks the women
-- and each woman strictly ranks the men, so "most preferred remaining" and "prefers m to my partner" are
-- unambiguous (no ties); (2) the **deferred-acceptance rule** — a woman holding a man releases him only for a man she
-- strictly prefers, and a man proposes to women in strict decreasing order of his preference and never re-proposes to
-- one who rejected him; (3) a **complete (quiescent) run** — the proposal schedule runs until no unengaged man has any
-- un-proposed woman left. Assumption (3) is the load-bearing admissibility hypothesis, and dropping it is exactly how
-- a blocking pair survives (a man who never got to propose to a woman he prefers). Surface where each is used. Keep
-- the two sides as arbitrary finite carriers and each agent's preference as a decidable strict linear order over the
-- opposite side; do **not** fix a decidable finite instance, and do not restrict to a single proposal step or a
-- two-agent market — the quantification over an arbitrary complete run is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap.
-- Probe the banked DeFi/AMM/CLOB `List.foldl` reachable-state invariant pattern for the deferred-acceptance induction.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- gale_shapley_stable_matching_theory.lean
--
-- ## Property class
-- SAFETY. The Target is an invariant of the terminal reachable state — the quiescent matching admits no blocking
-- pair — proved by induction over the proposal schedule (the DeFi/AMM/CLOB `List.foldl` shape). The **LIVENESS** dual
-- is deliberately **not** proven: that a quiescent state is always reached (deferred acceptance terminates, so a
-- complete stable matching always exists). Existence-via-termination is the frontier the library has not yet closed;
-- this target assumes a run reaches quiescence and characterizes what that terminal state guarantees.
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Man / Woman**: the two finite sides of the market (the proposing side and the receiving side).
-- - **prefM / prefW**: `prefM m x y` means man `m` strictly prefers woman `x` to woman `y`; `prefW w a b` means woman
--   `w` strictly prefers man `a` to man `b`. Each is a **strict linear order over the opposite side** — irreflexive,
--   transitive, and total on distinct agents (any two distinct alternatives are comparable) — and **decidable**, so
--   the choice tests below `REDUCE` rather than sitting behind an opaque `∃`.
-- - **chooseBetterForW**: given a woman `w` and two men, the man `w` prefers — a **plain computable `def`** by a
--   direct `if` on the decidable `prefW` (so `simp [chooseBetterForW]` / `if_pos` reduce it). It returns one of the
--   two men, never a third.
-- - **Matching**: an assignment `held : Woman → Option Man` (the man a woman currently holds, or none) in which no man
--   is held by two women — the deferred-acceptance process maintains this injectivity, since a man proposes only while
--   unheld. **partnerOfMan**: the woman holding a given man, or none (well-defined by that injectivity).
-- - **freeMan**: a man no woman currently holds.
-- - **BlockingPair**: a man `m` and woman `w` such that `m` strictly prefers `w` to `partnerOfMan m` (or `m` is a
--   freeMan) **and** `w` strictly prefers `m` to `held w` (or `w` holds no one) — both would defect from the match to
--   pair with each other. Formalize it as a **decidable** predicate on the two `Option` partners (a `Bool`/`Decidable
--   Prop` that reduces), never an opaque existential.
-- - **Stable**: a matching with **no** blocking pair.
-- - **ProposalState**: the deferred-acceptance state — the current `held : Woman → Option Man` together with, for each
--   man, `rem : Man → List Woman`, the women he has **not yet** proposed to, in his strict preference order.
-- - **openingState**: every woman holds no one (`held w = none`) and every man's `rem` is his full preference-ordered
--   list of women.
-- - **proposalStep**: a **plain computable `def`** advancing one proposal — given a freeMan `m` whose `rem m` is
--   nonempty, `m` proposes to its head `w`; `w` becomes `chooseBetterForW w` applied to her current holder and `m`
--   (keeping the better, rejecting the other); `rem m` drops its head. A step that names an ineligible man is the
--   identity. Define it by a **direct `if`** on the decidable freeMan/`rem` tests so it unfolds definitionally.
-- - **postProposals**: apply a finite proposal **schedule** (a `List Man`, the order in which men are activated to
--   make their next proposal) to a state in order — a left fold of `proposalStep`.
-- - **reachable**: a state equal to `postProposals sched openingState` for some finite schedule `sched`.
-- - **Quiescent**: a state in which **no** freeMan has a nonempty `rem` — every man is either held by a woman or has
--   exhausted his preference list. The completeness hypothesis of the Target.
--
-- ## Anchors (prove these — they PIN each def's meaning; a representation-dependent def cannot prove them)
-- - **chooseBetterForW returns the woman's genuine preference-maximum of the two**: for any woman `w` and men `a`, `b`,
--   `chooseBetterForW w a b` is one of `a`, `b`, and `w` weakly prefers it to both. A positional / first-argument
--   choice cannot prove this — the anchor forces the preference-driven selection, the analog of `bestBid` being the

structure StrictPreference (Agent : Type u) (Alt : Type v) where
  pref : Agent → Alt → Alt → Prop
  decidablePref : ∀ agent x y, Decidable (pref agent x y)
  irrefl : ∀ agent x, ¬ pref agent x x
  trans : ∀ agent {x y z}, pref agent x y → pref agent y z → pref agent x z
  total : ∀ agent {x y}, x ≠ y → pref agent x y ∨ pref agent y x

def WeaklyPrefers (prefs : StrictPreference Agent Alt)
    (agent : Agent) (x y : Alt) : Prop :=
  x = y ∨ prefs.pref agent x y

def chooseBetterForW (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (w : Woman) (a b : Man) : Man :=
  letI : Decidable (prefW.pref w a b) := prefW.decidablePref w a b
  if prefW.pref w a b then a else b

structure Matching (Man : Type u) (Woman : Type v) where
  held : Woman → Option Man

/-- No man is held by two different women. -/

def NoDuplicateHolds (μ : Matching Man Woman) : Prop :=
  ∀ {w₁ w₂ : Woman} {m : Man}, μ.held w₁ = some m → μ.held w₂ = some m → w₁ = w₂

def emptyMatching : Matching Man Woman :=
  { held := fun _ => none }

def freeMan [DecidableEq Man] (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : Woman, μ.held w ≠ some m

instance instDecidableFreeMan [Fintype Woman] [DecidableEq Man]
    (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Decidable (freeMan μ m) := by
  unfold freeMan
  infer_instance

noncomputable def partnerOfMan (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Option Woman :=
  by
    classical
    exact if h : ∃ w : Woman, μ.held w = some m then some (Classical.choose h) else none

def updateHeld [DecidableEq Woman]
    (held : Woman → Option Man) (w : Woman) (newHeld : Option Man) :
    Woman → Option Man :=
  fun w' => if w' = w then newHeld else held w'

def ManPrefersOption (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman)
    (m : Man) (w : Woman) : Option Woman → Prop
  | none => True
  | some w' => prefM.pref m w w'

instance instDecidableManPrefersOption
    (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman) (m : Man) (w : Woman) (partner : Option Woman) :
    Decidable (ManPrefersOption prefM m w partner) := by
  cases partner with
  | none => exact isTrue trivial
  | some w' => exact prefM.decidablePref m w w'

def WomanPrefersOption (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (w : Woman) (m : Man) : Option Man → Prop
  | none => True
  | some m' => prefW.pref w m m'

instance instDecidableWomanPrefersOption
    (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man) (w : Woman) (m : Man) (partner : Option Man) :
    Decidable (WomanPrefersOption prefW w m partner) := by
  cases partner with
  | none => exact isTrue trivial
  | some m' => exact prefW.decidablePref w m m'

noncomputable def ManPrefersCurrent [DecidableEq Man]
    (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman) (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) (w : Woman) :
    Prop :=
  ManPrefersOption prefM m w (partnerOfMan μ m)

noncomputable def BlockingPair [DecidableEq Man]
    (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman) (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) (w : Woman) : Prop :=
  ManPrefersCurrent prefM μ m w ∧ WomanPrefersOption prefW w m (μ.held w)

noncomputable def Stable [DecidableEq Man]
    (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman) (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (μ : Matching Man Woman) : Prop :=
  ∀ m w, ¬ BlockingPair prefM prefW μ m w

structure ProposalState (Man : Type u) (Woman : Type v) where
  matching : Matching Man Woman
  rem : Man → List Woman

/-- The opening state: nobody is held, and every man has his full proposal list. -/

def openingState (fullList : Man → List Woman) : ProposalState Man Woman :=
  { matching := emptyMatching, rem := fullList }

def ProposalListOrdered (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman)
    (m : Man) (women : List Woman) : Prop :=
  women.Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => prefM.pref m w₁ w₂)

def ProposalListsSound (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman)
    (fullList : Man → List Woman) : Prop :=
  ∀ m, (fullList m).Nodup ∧ ProposalListOrdered prefM m (fullList m)

def FreeManIn (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : Woman, μ.held w ≠ some m

def ProposalStepRel (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (state : ProposalState Man Woman) (m : Man) (next : ProposalState Man Woman) : Prop :=
  (¬ FreeManIn state.matching m ∧ next = state) ∨
    (FreeManIn state.matching m ∧ state.rem m = [] ∧ next = state) ∨
      ∃ w tail,
        FreeManIn state.matching m ∧
          state.rem m = w :: tail ∧
            ((state.matching.held w = none ∧ next.matching.held w = some m) ∨
              ∃ old,
                state.matching.held w = some old ∧
                  next.matching.held w = some (chooseBetterForW prefW w m old)) ∧
              (∀ w', w' ≠ w → next.matching.held w' = state.matching.held w') ∧
                next.rem m = tail ∧
                  ∀ m', m' ≠ m → next.rem m' = state.rem m'

inductive ProposalRun (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man) :
    ProposalState Man Woman → List Man → ProposalState Man Woman → Prop
  | nil (state : ProposalState Man Woman) : ProposalRun prefW state [] state
  | cons {state mid final : ProposalState Man Woman} {m : Man} {schedule : List Man} :
      ProposalStepRel prefW state m mid →
        ProposalRun prefW mid schedule final →
          ProposalRun prefW state (m :: schedule) final

                · simp [h]

  rem : Man → List Woman

  women.Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => prefM.pref m w₁ w₂)

  ∀ m, (fullList m).Nodup ∧ ProposalListOrdered prefM m (fullList m)

  ∀ w : Woman, μ.held w ≠ some m

    (state : ProposalState Man Woman) (m : Man) (next : ProposalState Man Woman) : Prop :=
  (¬ FreeManIn state.matching m ∧ next = state) ∨

      ∃ w tail,
        FreeManIn state.matching m ∧

              ∃ old,
                state.matching.held w = some old ∧

import Mathlib

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false

namespace GaleShapleyStableMatchingProbe

universe u v

structure StrictPreference (Agent : Type u) (Alt : Type v) where
  pref : Agent → Alt → Alt → Prop
  decidablePref : ∀ agent x y, Decidable (pref agent x y)
  irrefl : ∀ agent x, ¬ pref agent x x
  trans : ∀ agent {x y z}, pref agent x y → pref agent y z → pref agent x z
  total : ∀ agent {x y}, x ≠ y → pref agent x y ∨ pref agent y x

def WeaklyPrefers (prefs : StrictPreference Agent Alt)
    (agent : Agent) (x y : Alt) : Prop :=
  x = y ∨ prefs.pref agent x y

def chooseBetterForW (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (w : Woman) (a b : Man) : Man :=
  letI : Decidable (prefW.pref w a b) := prefW.decidablePref w a b
  if prefW.pref w a b then a else b

structure Matching (Man : Type u) (Woman : Type v) where
  held : Woman → Option Man

/-- No man is held by two different women. -/

def NoDuplicateHolds (μ : Matching Man Woman) : Prop :=
  ∀ {w₁ w₂ : Woman} {m : Man}, μ.held w₁ = some m → μ.held w₂ = some m → w₁ = w₂

def emptyMatching : Matching Man Woman :=
  { held := fun _ => none }

def freeMan [DecidableEq Man] (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : Woman, μ.held w ≠ some m

instance instDecidableFreeMan [Fintype Woman] [DecidableEq Man]
    (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Decidable (freeMan μ m) := by
  unfold freeMan
  infer_instance

noncomputable def partnerOfMan (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Option Woman :=
  by
    classical
    exact if h : ∃ w : Woman, μ.held w = some m then some (Classical.choose h) else none

def FreeManIn (μ : Matching Man Woman) (m : Man) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : Woman, μ.held w ≠ some m

structure ProposalState (Man : Type u) (Woman : Type v) where
  matching : Matching Man Woman
  rem : Man → List Woman

/-- The opening state: nobody is held, and every man has his full proposal list. -/

def openingState (fullList : Man → List Woman) : ProposalState Man Woman :=
  { matching := emptyMatching, rem := fullList }

def ProposalStepRel (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man)
    (state : ProposalState Man Woman) (m : Man) (next : ProposalState Man Woman) : Prop :=
  (¬ FreeManIn state.matching m ∧ next = state) ∨
    (FreeManIn state.matching m ∧ state.rem m = [] ∧ next = state) ∨
      ∃ w tail,
        FreeManIn state.matching m ∧
          state.rem m = w :: tail ∧
            ((state.matching.held w = none ∧ next.matching.held w = some m) ∨
              ∃ old,
                state.matching.held w = some old ∧
                  next.matching.held w = some (chooseBetterForW prefW w m old)) ∧
              (∀ w', w' ≠ w → next.matching.held w' = state.matching.held w') ∧
                next.rem m = tail ∧
                  ∀ m', m' ≠ m → next.rem m' = state.rem m'

inductive ProposalRun (prefW : StrictPreference Woman Man) :
    ProposalState Man Woman → List Man → ProposalState Man Woman → Prop
  | nil (state : ProposalState Man Woman) : ProposalRun prefW state [] state
  | cons {state mid final : ProposalState Man Woman} {m : Man} {schedule : List Man} :
      ProposalStepRel prefW state m mid →
        ProposalRun prefW mid schedule final →
          ProposalRun prefW state (m :: schedule) final

def ProposalListOrdered (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman)
    (m : Man) (women : List Woman) : Prop :=
  women.Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => prefM.pref m w₁ w₂)

def ProposalListsSound (prefM : StrictPreference Man Woman)
    (fullList : Man → List Woman) : Prop :=
  ∀ m, (fullList m).Nodup ∧ ProposalListOrdered prefM m (fullList m)

-- APPROACH (advisory blueprint / proof-idea guidance; the kernel verifies every step):
-- # Stable matching — deferred acceptance produces a matching with no blocking pair, across any complete proposal run
--
-- Opens the **market design / two-sided matching** frontier — the mechanism that clears the medical-residency match
-- (NRMP), public-school choice, and kidney exchange, and the one whose "intent" is contested in court and in policy
-- (the NRMP faced antitrust litigation over exactly what the match guarantees). The iconic result is Gale–Shapley:
-- run the deferred-acceptance procedure — each unengaged agent proposes down its preference list, each receiver keeps
-- its best proposer so far and rejects the rest — and the outcome is **stable**: no man and woman both strictly
-- prefer each other to the partner the match assigned them. Stability is the property the field means by "the match
-- is fair to participants," and it is what makes a centralized clearinghouse hold together against side deals. This is
-- the library's first result over an **iterative allocation process whose invariant is a monotone tentative
-- assignment** — the deferred-acceptance reachable-state induction, a discrete counterpart of the CLOB matching
-- engine, over preference orders rather than prices.
--
-- Assumption-accounting note: the results depend on (1) **strict preferences** — each man strictly ranks the women
-- and each woman strictly ranks the men, so "most preferred remaining" and "prefers m to my partner" are
-- unambiguous (no ties); (2) the **deferred-acceptance rule** — a woman holding a man releases him only for a man she
-- strictly prefers, and a man proposes to women in strict decreasing order of his preference and never re-proposes to
-- one who rejected him; (3) a **complete (quiescent) run** — the proposal schedule runs until no unengaged man has any
-- un-proposed woman left. Assumption (3) is the load-bearing admissibility hypothesis, and dropping it is exactly how
-- a blocking pair survives (a man who never got to propose to a woman he prefers). Surface where each is used. Keep
-- the two sides as arbitrary finite carriers and each agent's preference as a decidable strict linear order over the
-- opposite side; do **not** fix a decidable finite instance, and do not restrict to a single proposal step or a
-- two-agent market — the quantification over an arbitrary complete run is the point. A non-closure is an honest gap.
-- Probe the banked DeFi/AMM/CLOB `List.foldl` reachable-state invariant pattern for the deferred-acceptance induction.
--
-- ## Domain
-- formalization-nonmath
--
-- ## Theory file
-- gale_shapley_stable_matching_theory.lean
--
-- ## Property class
-- SAFETY. The Target is an invariant of the terminal reachable state — the quiescent matching admits no blocking
-- pair — proved by induction over the proposal schedule (the DeFi/AMM/CLOB `List.foldl` shape). The **LIVENESS** dual
-- is deliberately **not** proven: that a quiescent state is always reached (deferred acceptance terminates, so a
-- complete stable matching always exists). Existence-via-termination is the frontier the library has not yet closed;
-- this target assumes a run reaches quiescence and characterizes what that terminal state guarantees.
--
-- ## Vocabulary (build these as definitions — do not prove them)
-- - **Man / Woman**: the two finite sides of the market (the proposing side and the receiving side).
-- - **prefM / prefW**: `prefM m x y` means man `m` strictly prefers woman `x` to woman `y`; `prefW w a b` means woman
--   `w` strictly prefers man `a` to man `b`. Each is a **strict linear order over the opposite side** — irreflexive,
--   transitive, and total on distinct agents (any two distinct alternatives are comparable) — and **decidable**, so
--   the choice tests below `REDUCE` rather than sitting behind an opaque `∃`.
-- - **chooseBetterForW**: given a woman `w` and two men, the man `w` prefers — a **plain computable `def`** by a
--   direct `if` on the decidable `prefW` (so `simp [chooseBetterForW]` / `if_pos` reduce it). It returns one of the
--   two men, never a third.
-- - **Matching**: an assignment `held : Woman → Option Man` (the man a woman currently holds, or none) in which no man
--   is held by two women — the deferred-acceptance process maintains this injectivity, since a man proposes only while
--   unheld. **partnerOfMan**: the woman holding a given man, or none (well-defined by that injectivity).
-- - **freeMan**: a man no woman currently holds.
-- - **BlockingPair**: a man `m` and woman `w` such that `m` strictly prefers `w` to `partnerOfMan m` (or `m` is a
--   freeMan) **and** `w` strictly prefers `m` to `held w` (or `w` holds no one) — both would defect from the match to
--   pair with each other. Formalize it as a **decidable** predicate on the two `Option` partners (a `Bool`/`Decidable
--   Prop` that reduces), never an opaque existential.
-- - **Stable**: a matching with **no** blocking pair.
-- - **ProposalState**: the deferred-acceptance state — the current `held : Woman → Option Man` together with, for each
--   man, `rem : Man → List Woman`, the women he has **not yet** proposed to, in his strict preference order.
-- - **openingState**: every woman holds no one (`held w = none`) and every man's `rem` is his full preference-ordered
--   list of **all** women (preferences are complete, so his ranking exhausts the whole opposite side).
-- - **proposalStep**: a **plain computable `def`** advancing one proposal — given a freeMan `m` whose `rem m` is
--   nonempty, `m` proposes to its head `w`; `w` becomes `chooseBetterForW w` applied to her current holder and `m`
--   (keeping the better, rejecting the other); `rem m` drops its head. A step that names an ineligible man is the
--   identity. Define it by a **direct `if`** on the decidable freeMan/`rem` tests so it unfolds definitionally.
-- - **postProposals**: apply a finite proposal **schedule** (a `List Man`, the order in which men are activated to
--   make their next proposal) to a state in order — a left fold of `proposalStep`.
-- - **reachable**: a state equal to `postProposals sched openingState` for some finite schedule `sched`.
-- - **Quiescent**: a state in which **no** freeMan has a nonempty `rem` — every man is either held by a woman or has
--   exhausted his preference list. This is the complete-RUN hypothesis (the schedule reached a fixpoint) — it is DISTINCT from the complete-LIST hypothesis (every woman on every man's list) above; a complete run over a list that omits some woman still leaves a man who never proposed to her, so BOTH are required for stability.
--
-- ## Anchors (prove these — they PIN each def's meaning; a representation-dependent def cannot prove them)
-- - **chooseBetterForW returns the woman's genuine preference-maximum of the two**: for any woman `w` and men `a`, `b`,
--   `chooseBetterForW w a b` is one of `a`, `b`, and `w` weakly prefers it to both. A positional / first-argument
--   choice cannot prove this — the anchor forces the preference-driven selection, the analog of `bestBid` being the
--   max rather than a list head.
-- - **prefW / prefM are strict linear orders — comparability and no ties**: for distinct men `a`, `b`, exactly one of
--   `prefW w a b` and `prefW w b a` holds (symmetrically for `prefM`). This forces the total, tie-free preference
--   relation the "most preferred remaining" pointer and the blocking test rely on, over a merely partial or
--   positional ranking.
--
-- ## Target
-- Consider man-proposing deferred acceptance over two finite sides with strict preferences and **complete proposal lists** — each man's ranked list of women to propose to (his `rem` at the opening state) contains EVERY woman, so no woman is ever absent from any man's list and a man who has exhausted his list has genuinely proposed to all of them (this list-completeness is a hypothesis on the LISTS, not merely the strictness/totality of the preference relation; without it a quiescent man can still strictly prefer a woman who was never on his list, and that pair blocks — so it is load-bearing): starting from the empty
-- matching, unengaged men propose to women in strict order of preference, and each woman tentatively holds the best
-- proposer she has seen and rejects the rest, a held man being displaced only by one she strictly prefers. After
-- **any** finite proposal schedule that runs to quiescence — no unengaged man has an un-proposed woman left — the
-- resulting matching is **stable**: there is no blocking pair, i.e. no man and woman who each strictly prefer the
-- other to the partner the match assigned them. So the outcome of a complete deferred-acceptance run is immune to
-- pairwise defection. Surface that quiescence is load-bearing: an incomplete run can leave an unengaged man who
-- strictly prefers a woman he never reached, and that pair blocks — so stability is a property of the **completed**
-- run, not of an arbitrary partial one. (The dual guarantee that a quiescent state is always reached — termination
-- and hence existence of a stable matching — is the liveness result this target does not cover.)
--
-- ## Lemmas
-- - Along any proposal schedule from the opening state, a woman's held man is monotone under her preference: at any
--   reachable state she weakly prefers her held man to any man she held at an earlier reachable state, and once she
--   holds a man she is never again free.
-- - If a woman rejects a man at some reachable state — she keeps or takes another over him — then at every later
--   reachable state she holds a man she strictly prefers to the one she rejected.
-- - The women a man has already proposed to form an initial segment of his preference order at every reachable state;
--   in particular, at a quiescent state a man has proposed to every woman he strictly prefers to his own assigned
--   partner (and to every woman, if he is unengaged).
-- - At a quiescent reachable state, GIVEN complete proposal lists (each man's list ranks EVERY woman, so a quiescent man has genuinely proposed to all women, not merely a subset — without this a quiescent man can still strictly prefer a woman never on his list and that pair blocks), the matching is stable: for every man `m` and woman `w`, they are not a blocking
--   pair — the completed run leaves no pair who would both defect to each other.
-- - Quiescence is load-bearing: there is a profile and a non-quiescent reachable state whose matching has a blocking
--   pair, so the quiescence hypothesis in the stability claim cannot be dropped.
--
-- ## Idea
-- Everything runs over `reachable` states obtained by `List.foldl proposalStep` from `openingState` — the same
-- reachable-state shape as the banked DeFi admissible-sequence and CLOB matching-engine invariants, so mirror them:
-- induct on the schedule, and at each `proposalStep` the woman it touches either keeps her holder or replaces it by
-- `chooseBetterForW`, which the anchor pins to be weakly better — the woman-improvement invariant is that monotonicity
-- carried along the fold. The rejected-dominated lemma is the same invariant read at a rejection: `chooseBetterForW`
-- kept a man she prefers to the rejected one, and monotonicity carries it forward. The initial-segment lemma is
-- structural: `rem m` starts as `m`'s full preference-ordered list and `proposalStep` drops only its head, so the
-- proposed set is exactly the complement prefix. Stability at quiescence combines them: if `m` strictly prefers `w` to
-- his partner then by the initial-segment lemma `m` proposed to `w`, and — since he is not held by her — she rejected
-- him, so by the rejected-dominated lemma she holds a man she strictly prefers to `m`; hence `w` does not prefer `m`
-- to her partner and `(m, w)` is no blocking pair. The load-bearing witness is a small explicit market (a couple of
-- men and women) run one step short of quiescence, exhibiting a surviving blocking pair. Probe Mathlib's `List.foldl`
-- and `List` prefix lemmas and the order/decidability machinery; keep the two sides as finite parameters and the
-- preferences as decidable strict linear orders, and do not fix a decidable carrier or collapse the schedule to a
-- single step. This is a frontier target — the quiescent-stability capstone is a real lift; the woman-improvement
-- invariant, the rejected-dominated lemma, and the load-bearing witness are the reachable-state-invariant spine the
-- engine already nails if the capstone resists.
--

-- # Gale-Shapley deferred acceptance substrate

-- This file records the formal substrate for a man-proposing deferred acceptance
-- campaign.  The first pass deliberately keeps the mechanism data ordinary:
-- preferences are strict decidable relations, a matching is an assignment from
-- women to optional men, and proposal states carry the current held assignment
